clue.text: Twirling journalist wearing clown's suit

indicators.note: twirling spins the whole assembled group of letters round so it reads from the other end
the journalist is worn by the clown, so sits inside those letters

parts.note: a clown is a sap, a fool; clown's gives saps, the word with its S
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A spinning reporter dressed up in a circus clown's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing beside 'clown', but it is the card suit; 'Twirling' reverses the whole SEDAPS. A clown is a sap, a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Card games have four suits, and the black one shaped like a pointed leaf is one of them.

clue.text: Left idea for saucy yarn's beginning with one's newspaper

parts.note: pro means in favour of
pert means cheeky or saucy

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of the word yarn

parts.note: one is I, and 's is 'is', together read as I-S
the FT, the Financial Times, read with its article

explanation.surface: A left-wing notion for a racy story, opening with a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left idea' is a left-wing idea: Proudhon's anarchist slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The French anarchist Proudhon coined this slogan, a radical left-wing principle against private ownership.

clue.text: Like some computers? Very nearly like the whole lot!

indicators.note: very nearly means stop one letter short of the full phrase

parts.note: 'dig it all': dig is slang for like, so enjoying the lot

explanation.surface: A playful remark about computers, and about liking everything.
explanation.walkthrough: DIG IT ALL, slang for liking the whole lot, loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern computers process information as binary numbers, unlike older analogue machines, so they are described this way.

clue.text: Flora and Johnny involved in fling

indicators.note: the Johnny is involved in the fling, so sits inside it

parts.note: to shy is to throw or fling
a johnny is British slang for a condom, a rubber

explanation.surface: Flora and Johnny are caught up in a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' and 'Johnny' look like a couple, but Flora is plant life and a johnny is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora means plant life, and a mass of bushes is exactly such planting.

clue.text: Explorer back in country, one caught spying on royalty

parts.note: Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller to China

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little word beside it the other way round

parts.note: US, the United States

explanation.surface: An adventurer returns home and is arrested as a spy on the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long description from Hamlet, not a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet the old courtier hides behind the arras to eavesdrop on the prince and queen and is stabbed there.

clue.text: Criticise American pressure about promoting political unity

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: about turns the pressure unit round to read backwards

parts.note: the bar is a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: Attacking American lobbying over a push for political union.
explanation.definitionFit: This movement sought to unite all the Arabic-speaking nations politically, an adjective for that aim.

clue.text: Cruciverbalist's sidekick with some incredible wisdom

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crossword solver's assistant is credited with remarkable insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse, the TV detective, loved crosswords, and his sergeant was his loyal assistant.

clue.text: Tip for cooking, stuffing cut carp

indicators.note: the cooked tip is stuffing, so it goes inside the cut

parts.note: a nick is a small cut

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of tip are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: stuff a carp that has been cut open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish, but it is the verb. 'for cooking' rearranges the letters of tip into ITP before they are stuffed in.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain about trivial things, which is fussy fault-finding.

clue.text: Seek out cheerful, hazy line in futuristic picture

indicators.note: hazy suggests something confused and unclear, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Search for a happy, vague phrase in a science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Star Wars is set 'a long time ago', so 'futuristic' is loose but fair for its look.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi-Wan's voice urges the hero to trust his instincts in Star Wars, a famous quoted line.

clue.text: Acceptable payment to occupy empty London club

indicators.note: the two inner pieces move in and fill the space left by the emptied city name
empty means the city's name loses all its inside letters, leaving its two ends

parts.note: ON as in 'that's not on': allowed, acceptable
a giro is a payment by bank transfer, especially a UK benefit cheque

explanation.surface: Fair money moves into a vacant London gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outer L and N of London. The club is a golf club, not a Pall Mall institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry several irons, and the low-numbered ones for distance shots go by this name.

clue.text: Most of sheep in the rain? One of them

parts.note: anything out in the rain is wet

indicators.note: most of means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a herd is a group of animals, here of sheep

explanation.surface: A wry question about a flock caught in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheep in the rain are a WET HERD; 'Most of' drops the last D. 'them' refers back to the sheep, so the definition leans on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated ram is a particular kind of male sheep, so it is one of the flock.

clue.text: Conferred with footballer needing to be paid off?

parts.note: George, the Northern Irish winger who starred for Manchester United
a debt still outstanding is a sum due to someone

explanation.surface: Talks were held with a player who has debts to clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conferred' looks like 'consulted' beside 'with', but it is 'granted'. George Best was a famous, famously free-spending footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer an honour on someone is to give or grant it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Scots bash vessels navy moored in bay

indicators.note: the vessels and navy are moored in the bay, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a bight is a wide curving bay in a coastline
urns are vessels, containers

explanation.surface: Scots attack ships of a fleet anchored in a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a verb of attack, but it is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots celebrate the poet Robert Burns each 25 January with a supper of haggis and whisky, a famous party.

clue.text: PM losing head in conflict with European

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a battle is a conflict

explanation.surface: A prime minister loses his cool in a dispute with a European.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTLE without its head gives ATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the Labour Prime Minister of Britain from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: What makes baker stop

parts.note: take the word break and send it off, i.e. rearrange it, and it spells baker

explanation.surface: A riddle about what causes a baker to halt work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: BREAK, with OFF as an anagram signal, rearranges to BAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To end talks or a relationship abruptly is to halt it, a phrasal verb for stop.

clue.text: English wound up? In France, we could be easily aroused

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to gore is to wound with horns
nous is French for we

explanation.surface: An excited Englishman abroad confesses that the French are easily aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like excited, but it is a word for wound read upwards in this down clue. E follows it, though 'English' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Zones of the body sensitive to sexual stimulation are described this way, so they could be aroused.

clue.text: Verbally abuse Tory minister? Party leader's appalled

parts.note: to dis or diss someone is to insult them
Theresa May, Conservative cabinet minister at the time
Ed Miliband, then leader of the Labour Party; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A politician insults a Conservative minister and his party leader is horrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Being appalled means being filled with consternation and alarm, a close synonym.

clue.text: After 31 days, examination of a government official

indicators.note: after places the examination straight after the month

parts.note: May is a month of 31 days
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: After a month, a mayor faces an inspection by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the head of a town council, a local government official.

clue.text: Teacher, with age, defends right to be a bore

indicators.note: the teacher and age surround and protect the right, which sits inside

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: An older teacher defends the right to be tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at tedious length in a monotone is to bore one's listeners.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with car that's kind of blue

parts.note: O, the figure zero
X is the cross marking a wrong answer
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Nothing is wrong with a car described as a shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark blue is the university's colour, so a deep navy shade is named after it.

clue.text: Diver, turning up gold fish's head, fed

indicators.note: head picks out the first letter of fish
in a down clue, turning up means the gold is written bottom to top

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a fed is an American FBI agent, a G-man

explanation.surface: A diver finds gold and feeds a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' looks like the verb, but it is an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer working underwater in rubber suit and flippers is a type of diver.

clue.text: Reluctant to explore a hot and steamy novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who prefers reading a racy book to travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A homebody who never ventures out is unwilling to go exploring, the adjective for a person of that habit.

clue.text: Taunt a trio intermittently, giving musical instruction

indicators.note: intermittently takes every other letter of the words before it

explanation.surface: Mock a group of three musicians on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian direction on a score tells every performer to play together, a musical instruction.

clue.text: See 11
Not public school receiving royal backing

indicators.note: the school receives the royal letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought or belief

indicators.note: backing means the royal abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A private school gets royal patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not the education one but a sect; ER reversed is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden from general view is private and confidential, the opposite of public.

clue.text: Uncovered bird or rodent or mammoth

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters off the whole run of words

parts.note: a hen is a bird
a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A list of creatures, bird, rodent or prehistoric elephant, stripped bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' strips the outer ends off the whole run HEN OR MOUSE, so H and E go. 'mammoth' looks like the animal, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth used as an adjective means huge, a synonym for vast.

clue.text: Farm fertiliser has stable particle

parts.note: a stall is a compartment in a stable
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: Farm manure contains a steady particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fertiliser' looks like manure, but it is a breeding horse that fertilises mares.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding fertilises mares, so it is a witty farm fertiliser.

clue.text: Decline in the west has society getting soft

parts.note: something unset has not hardened, staying soft

explanation.surface: The decline of the West shows society going soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline in the west' reads as civilisation's fall, but it is the sun sinking in the western sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Each evening the sun goes down in the western sky, and that daily descent is this time of day.
